clue.text: Grave individual, fellow with the stuffing knocked out

parts.note: sole means single or individual

indicators.note: the inner filling of the word is knocked out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A serious-looking chap who seems deflated, as if the stuffing has been knocked out of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the stuffing knocked out' removes the middle A of MAN, leaving MN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and solemn are synonyms, both meaning serious in manner.

clue.text: Depression with pounds lost in financially challenging time

indicators.note: the pounds are lost from the word, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a slump is an economic downturn
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A gloomy depression during a recession when money is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like the economic sense, but it is a hollow or pit, as an engine's oil sump is.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a hollow or pit where liquid collects, a physical depression.

clue.text: Man facing endless prejudice when finally revealed as gay

parts.note: Les is a man's name, short for Leslie

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: bias is prejudice

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A man confronting bigotry as he comes out as gay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts BIAS to BIA; 'when finally' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesbian is a gay woman, so the word fits the adjective gay.

clue.text: Fashion designer — a black-looking fellow, inwardly bad

indicators.note: the word for bad is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a coal miner comes up from the pit blackened with dust
ill means bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: A designer described as a dark, sinister figure who is rotten inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black-looking fellow' suggests a villain; it is a miner covered in coal dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes and designs hats, a branch of fashion design.

clue.text: Philosophical outlook I peddle is mad, not of our era

parts.note: to deal is to peddle, especially drugs

indicators.note: AD (anno domini) marks our era, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone peddling a philosophy considered crazy and out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not of our era' removes AD from MAD, leaving M.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is a school of philosophy and also a general attitude of pursuing ideals.

clue.text: Doubles from boring bods in the belfry?

parts.note: dead means dull or boring
bell-ringers work in a church belfry; bods is British slang for people

explanation.surface: A question about doubles in bell-ringing coming from dull bell-ringers.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubles is also a bell-ringing method, which fits the belfry surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead ringers are people who look exactly alike, so they are each other's doubles.

clue.text: Plant book promoted before Christmas?

definitions.meaning: a plant that lives only one year
a yearly children's hardback, typically sold as a Christmas present in Britain

explanation.surface: A plant and a book both marketed in the run-up to Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a one-season plant and a yearly gift book published for the Christmas market.

clue.text: Rail taking home very small number, losing time

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the word loses the letter for time

parts.note: eight is a small number

explanation.surface: A railway line taking in a few homes but making slow progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' is a verb, to complain angrily, not a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail against something and to inveigh against it both mean to protest bitterly.

clue.text: The old woman hangs around and pretends to be ill

parts.note: ma is an informal word for one's mother, the old woman
lingers means hangs around

explanation.surface: Mother loiters about the house claiming to be sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Malingering is faking illness to avoid work or duty.

clue.text: Power of inspiring person engaging class

indicators.note: to engage here is to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a muse inspires an artist
CL is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: The influence of a charismatic teacher captivating a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle is used figuratively for power or clout.

clue.text: Four participating in sensual merriment

indicators.note: the numeral takes part within the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: carnal means sensual or fleshly
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A foursome joining in some fleshly fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a festive celebration, so it stands for revelry and merriment.

clue.text: Male is part of the group arranged to provide lies

parts.note: being in formation means arranged as part of a group, like aircraft or soldiers

explanation.surface: A man joins a group set up to spread falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: The last piece is read as two words, IN FORMATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Misinformation is false or misleading information, which amounts to lies.

clue.text: Foolish chat about educational establishment

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Silly talk concerning a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges FOOLISH CHAT; 'Foolish' looks like the signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A faith school is a religious school, an establishment for education.

clue.text: Well-placed religious institution that's pleasant, not cold, inside

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a convent is a religious community of nuns

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for cold is dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A nunnery that is handily located and agreeable, and warm inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' signals dropping the cold letter, and 'inside' places the trimmed word within the religious institution; 'Well-placed' sounds like a description of the convent but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Convenient means handily situated, so it is a synonym of well-placed.

clue.text: Abandon computers and suchlike? You must be joking!

parts.note: to come off something, such as a drug, is to give it up
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: An instruction to give up screens, met with disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Come off it is an informal exclamation of disbelief, like saying 'you can't be serious'.

clue.text: That place not right for you

indicators.note: not signals the letter for right is left out

parts.note: there means that place

explanation.surface: Telling someone a location is wrong for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the old object form of the second-person pronoun, so it stands for you.

clue.text: Show words inside book?

parts.note: the text of an opera or musical, which is printed in a little booklet; the word is Italian for little book

explanation.surface: A question about the words printed inside a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical, and its name means a small book.

clue.text: Revolutionary to spoil mark on ballot paper

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
voters mark their choice with a cross, X

explanation.surface: A radical voter spoils their ballot paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoiling a ballot paper, deliberately marking it wrongly, is a protest vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx was a revolutionary thinker whose ideas inspired communist revolutions.

clue.text: More than one puzzle rankles, spread across days and days

indicators.note: the first word spreads itself across the two letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to rile is to annoy, as something that rankles does
D is the abbreviation for day
D again for the second day

explanation.surface: A grudge that festers for days on end.
explanation.walkthrough: The singular verb 'rankles' gives RILES, which surrounds DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddles are puzzling questions, so the plural fits more than one puzzle.

clue.text: Good humour shown by 19 22 against English in game

indicators.note: the combined pieces go in the name of the game

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: against means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: the answer to 19 and 22 is a name for Ireland, whose poetic name is Erin

explanation.surface: Irish good cheer facing the English in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference: '19 22' stands for the answer to that clue, a name for Ireland, and Erin is Ireland's poetic name. 'against' means next to; 'in' puts the pair within the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeriness is cheerfulness, a state of good humour.

clue.text: Land across the water in which you may see leader smile

indicators.note: the answer is a place in which the letters of the following words may be seen rearranged

explanation.surface: A country overseas where the leader may be seen smiling.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is unusual: the letters of LEADER SMILE can be seen in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emerald Isle is Ireland, a land across the Irish Sea from Britain.

clue.text: Picture maker arrived — famous painter?

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, an eminent British artist

explanation.surface: A question whether a famous artist has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera makes pictures, as photographs.

clue.text: Government agency working undercover, say, with unknown number involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up in, so the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
working means in operation, so these letters are put to work in a new order

parts.note: N is the algebraic symbol for an unknown number

explanation.surface: A government body operating covertly with an unknown number of agents.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is the British national mapping agency; the spy surface misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ordnance Survey is the UK government body that produces official maps.

clue.text: See 19
Idiot hugging tree, expressing a load of nonsense?

indicators.note: the word for idiot hugs the other piece inside it

parts.note: a fool is an idiot

indicators.note: read as ex-pressing, pressing out, so the letter A is squeezed out

parts.note: an alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree-hugging fool spouting rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing' is split as ex-pressing, pressing out, so the 'a' is squeezed out of the tree; 'hugging' puts what remains inside the idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Folderol is foolish talk or fuss, so it means a load of rubbish.

clue.text: Mathematical info about old animals

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: stats are statistics, mathematical information

explanation.surface: Statistical data about animals from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoats are small carnivorous mammals of the weasel family.

clue.text: What scientific theory may be established in columnar layout?

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the word for the layout

parts.note: a table sets data out in columns
EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A scientific theory established by data presented in a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientific theory should be open to experimental checking, as Popper argued.

clue.text: Dog mess lazy one leaves

parts.note: poo is the mess a dog makes

indicators.note: the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: idle means lazy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dog leaves its mess and a lazy person walks off.
explanation.definitionFit: The poodle is a breed of dog.
